name: Technology Entrepreneurship
description: Provides engineering students with training at the interface of engineering and technology development, emphasizing translating technical ideas into practical applications in technology-driven ventures, mission-oriented projects, and innovation within industry, government, and research institutions.
notes: Participating majors: Biomedical Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Minimum grade C in each course; all courses taken for a letter grade
Attend and participate in three experiential units (internship, Hillhouse Fellows, Engineering Dean's Speaker Series, or Tsai City Accelerator) with a 1–2 page write-up for each
No more than two course credits may overlap with a major, simultaneous degree, or another certificate
No course credit may count toward more than two curricular programs
Approved graduate and professional school courses may count
Non-Yale courses may not count without prior director approval
Submit application with major, tentative coursework plan, and faculty evaluators; director adds requirements to Degree Audit upon approval
